counterfactual_missing_items: Explicit leukocytoclasis/nuclear dust is not reported
decisive_items: Intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with marked papillary dermal edema, necrosis of vessel walls, and focal fibrinoid necrosis
multiple discrete, round, dry ulcers, most with central eschars, dusky gray borders, and collarettes of scale
response.rationale: R4 best integrates the raw histology: perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate, vessel-wall necrosis, and fibrinoid necrosis define cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis, with the leg ulcer morphology and MPO-ANCA positivity as supporting context. R5 is a broader but correct umbrella; C1 is simply an append-only restatement of the histopathology and is discounted. R1 lacks granulomatous disease evidence, R2 lacks medium-vessel arteritis, R3 rests only on low-titer ANA, and R6 requires panniculitis/TB.

rejected.why: Append-only completion of R5; label restates raw histology rather than being an independent diagnostic entity, so it is discounted as a correlated restatement.
No granulomatous inflammation or airway/renal evidence; P-ANCA 1:20 is borderline and MPO-ANCA is not specific for Wegener/GPA.
Histology shows dermal small-vessel perivascular vasculitis with papillary dermal edema, not medium-vessel arteritis typical of polyarteritis nodosa.
Only low-titer ANA 1:80 and anti-SSA with normal complement; lacks SLE criteria and is better explained by leukocytoclastic/ANCA-associated vasculitis.
Erythema induratum requires lobular panniculitis/granulomatous inflammation and often TB association; biopsy and stains do not support panniculitis.
